checkpoints.description: [1/1] fix the comparison-branch lowering so a left operand held in a temporary register is the one compared, then pin it with a runtime test and a shape test and record the ADR

impact_assessment.why: a miscompile: _emit_comparison_branch calls _emit_left_operand then always compares rcx, but _emit_left_operand puts a non-leaf right operand's left value in a temporary and sets left_hold, so the branch compared a stale rcx (if t > (i & 65535) with t negative took the true branch; the value form of the same compare was correct)
impact_assessment.benefits: correct control flow for every if/while whose comparison has a non-leaf right operand and a non-leaf left operand; the value-form and branch-form lowerings then agree
impact_assessment.risks: contract: generated bytes change only at such compares; dependency: none; concurrency: cairn tree is clean and no other task is active; state: ledger only
impact_assessment.mitigation: honour left_hold exactly as _emit_binary already does, pin the shape and the runtime answer, run the full suite and the benchmark diff

checkpoints.description: [1/1] committed as cceebbd: _emit_comparison_branch now consumes self.left_hold and clears it before cmp, falling back to rcx, so a left value parked in a temporary by a non-leaf right operand is the one branched on; failing-first proof on HEAD showed all three new tests failing (end-to-end 1/4/5 against the correct 2/3/0), with all three passing after the fix; full suite 1366 OK; 5/5 project gates passed; ADR-090 records the fix and the two G-004 benchmark runs that read +9.6 to +613 percent under host contention (compile times ~10x, short cases worst) with the clean 17a5e10 baseline restored and the loaded logs kept outside the tree; no speed claim; checklists: passed
